Maintenance Report — MNT-0200-009

Asset: WELL-0200 (NE-08 Well 200, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 17 May 2024 08:00 · Finished: 28 May 2024 12:00 · Well stopped for this job: 268 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Kevin Price, Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0200-0083 on 2024-05-16 Report written: 30 May 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that oil was dripping from the gearbox onto the pump jack base. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0200-0083 showed the wellhead at 36.7 °C with the air at 28.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 9 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

A hardened output shaft seal after years of service.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0200-009; the manifest was only completed the following week (WS-06).

Parts and cost

ItemUSD
Gearbox seal kit624
Gear oil554
Absorbent pads208
Labour (company crew)874
Total2,260

Compliance check

ProtocolResultDetail

WS-07MetWritten 2 days after the work (limit 3 days)

Notes and recommendations

  • Check the gearbox oil level monthly on this unit.
  • Used oil and pads shipped as oily waste.
  • HSE to follow up on the WS-06 item above with the crew.

maintenance.action: Replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0200-012

Asset: WELL-0200 (NE-08 Well 200, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 22 Sep 2024 08:00 · Finished: 15 Oct 2024 12:00 · Well stopped for this job: 556 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0200-0101 on 2024-09-19 Report written: 16 Oct 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the electric motor driving the pump jack had stopped and would not restart. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0200-0101 showed the wellhead at 35.3 °C with the air at 28.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 21 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Winding breakdown from heat and age.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

Notes and recommendations

  • Clean the motor cooling fins at each scheduled service.
  • Summer heat raises the risk of motor trips on this field.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0200-018

Asset: WELL-0200 (NE-08 Well 200, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: wellhead Work started: 17 Oct 2025 08:00 · Finished: 26 Nov 2025 16:00 · Well stopped for this job: 968 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Kevin Price · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0200-0155 on 2025-10-16 Report written: 26 Nov 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that fluid was weeping from the stuffing box around the polished rod. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0200-0155 showed the wellhead at 25.0 °C with the air at 19.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The packing rings were worn and the polished rod was lightly scored. The well stayed shut in for about 38 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Packing wear sped up by a slightly misaligned polished rod.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Closed the wellhead valves and bled off pressure.
  2. Removed the old packing.
  3. Installed new packing rings and adjusted the gland.
  4. Cleaned the wellhead area.

Summary of the fix: replaced stuffing box packing.

Testing and return to service

Checked the stuffing box with the unit running: no leak. The well was returned to production.
